key: Deemed ye then that We had created you for naught, and that ye would not be returned unto Us?
s: After the doomed are told they tarried on earth but a little, God questions them; al-Tabari, on 23:114 to 23:115, takes it as asking the wretched whether they thought themselves made in play and falsehood, not to live again and be repaid for their deeds.

evidence.words: يقول تعالى ذكره: أفحسبتم أيها الأشقياء أنا إنما خلقناكم إذ خلقناكم، لعبا وباطلا وأنكم إلى ربكم بعد مماتكم لا تصيرون أحياء، فتجزون بما كنتم في الدنيا تعملون
evidence.gloss: God, exalted be His mention, says: Did you then reckon, O wretched ones, that when We created you We created you only in play and falsehood, and that after your death you would not come back living to your Lord, to be repaid for what you used to do in the world?

reason: The problem holds: day 53 (41:34, al-Tabari: repel offence with pardon till the foe is like a near kinsman) and this entry (23:96, Ibn Kathir: good done to the wrongdoer until enmity turns to friendship) teach the same line fifteen days apart. Moved the key verse to 23:115 (verse.js ok, Al-Mu’minun 23:115, at 2787), which no other day in the batch uses. Opened al-Tabari on 23:114 to 23:115 (packet.js quran 38 --verse 23.115): on 23:114 he glosses the answer as God telling them they stayed on earth but a short while, and on 23:115 he says in his own voice that God asks the wretched (al-ashqiya) whether they thought He created them in play and falsehood (la‘iban wa-batilan), and that after death they would not come back alive to their Lord to be repaid for what they did in the world. The reading paraphrases that and no more; his note on the two readings of turja‘un is not used. Plain sense from day.js 23:112 to 23:114 (asked how long they tarried, told it was but a little), no four-word run from the key verse. Commentator changed from Ibn Kathir to al-Tabari because the move was of the key verse and al-Tabari has the substantive gloss on it (the plan default). 44 words; entry-check ok.
